I have farmed this same 4.1 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I know this land like the back of my hand. I am 64 now and live alone, so I cannot chase the highest yields in the village anymore — I need a plan that is steady, saves my back, and does not require more labor than I can handle.

This year, I will plant the whole 4.1 mu to winter wheat after the autumn maize comes off. I will buy improved wheat seed from the supply store in town because it is reliable and I have used it for years. Before sowing, I will hire the village rotary tiller to prepare the seedbed. I will put down compound fertilizer as a base and top-dress urea in the spring when the wheat turns green. I have a well, so I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings survive the cold, once at jointing when the stems shoot up, and once at grain filling. I will spray herbicide after sowing and one fungicide in the spring if the weather turns damp. I expect about 450 kg per mu — not the best in the village, but consistent.

After the wheat harvest in early June, I will sow summer maize immediately on the same 4.1 mu. I will use hybrid seed; everyone around here uses hybrid maize, and I would be foolish not to. I will not till much — I will have the sowing machine plant directly into the wheat stubble to save time and because I do not have the strength to turn the soil twice in the heat of summer. I will put down fertilizer at sowing and add more nitrogen when the maize is knee-high. I will irrigate twice if the rain does not come: once to help emergence if the soil is dry, and once around the big喇叭口 stage. Two sprays: a herbicide at sowing and one insecticide when the borers usually appear in August. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

I keep my inputs modest because I farm alone and must control costs. I hire the machinery cooperative for plowing, harvesting, and sowing — I cannot lift bags of seed or wrestle with the equipment like I did 20 years ago. But my eyes are still good, and I walk the fields every morning. That is how I manage.
